updates.name: Adrienne J. Sutton
updates.bio: Oceanographer with NOAA's Pacific Marine Environmental Laboratory carbon group. She studies air-sea CO2 exchange and seawater carbonate chemistry across open-ocean, coastal and coral reef settings, using autonomous buoys and other platforms to separate natural variability (e.g. ENSO, reef metabolism) from long-term ocean carbon trends. PhD in oceanography, University of Maryland (2006).
updates.research_interests: air-sea CO2 exchange; ocean carbonate chemistry; ocean acidification in open-ocean, coastal and coral reef environments; ENSO and coral reef metabolism effects on carbon chemistry; autonomous buoy observations of long-term ocean carbon trends

updates.name: Anne E. Giblin
updates.bio: Senior scientist and Director of the Ecosystems Center at the Marine Biological Laboratory, and lead principal investigator of the Plum Island Ecosystems LTER. A biogeochemist, she studies how nitrogen, sulfur, iron and phosphorus cycle in sediments and soils, and how nutrient loading, hydrologic change and sea-level rise alter estuarine nitrogen and carbon cycling. PhD, Boston University Marine Program.
updates.research_interests: biogeochemistry of nitrogen, sulfur, iron and phosphorus; element cycling in sediments and soils under varying redox conditions; denitrification and nitrogen removal pathways; effects of nitrogen loading, hydrologic disturbance and sea-level rise on salt-marsh and estuarine N and C cycling; arctic lake and tundra nutrient cycling
